Surah Al-'Asr

There are two opinions concerning it.

The first is that it is Meccan. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr, and the majority.

The second is that it is Medinan. This was said by Mujahid, Qatadah, and Muqatil.

The words of the Exalted and Majestic: ﴿By time﴾ — concerning it there are three opinions.

The first: it is the age (al-dahr), said by Ibn 'Abbas, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Farra', and Ibn Qutaybah. God swore by the age because in it there is a lesson for the observer, in the passing of the night and the day according to a measure that does not fail.

The second: it is the afternoon (al-'ashiyy), which is the period between the decline of the sun and its setting. This was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah.

The third: it is the afternoon prayer (salat al-'asr). This was said by Muqatil.

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ — al-Zajjaj said: this is the answer to the oath.

Here "al-insan" (mankind) means "an-nas" (people), just as you say: "the dirham has become abundant in the hands of people," meaning the dirhams. "Al-khusr" and "al-khusran" have the same meaning. The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: "al-khusr" is the ruin or the diminishing of the capital. So when a person does not employ himself in that which brings him lasting profit, he is in loss, because he has worked toward the ruin of himself, and these two are the greatest of his capital. ﴿Except those who have believed﴾, that is: those who were truthful to God and His Messenger and acted in obedience. ﴿And advised each other to truth﴾, that is: to monotheism, the Qur'an, and following the Messenger. ﴿And advised each other to patience﴾ upon the obedience of God and the upholding of His law.

Ibrahim said in interpreting this surah: indeed, the person who is given a long life in this world is in a state of decline and weakness, except the believers, for they will be recorded the rewards of the deeds they used to do in their youth and their health.
